frozen_on: dev split only, before any TEST run at this configuration
rationale: Dense and BM25 are genuinely complementary on dev: of 14 answerable questions each retriever finds 3 that the other misses (union ceiling 0.857 vs 0.643 for either alone). Reciprocal rank fusion recovers most of that union at 0.786 while also lifting top-document accuracy from 0.357 (dense) to 0.571. Neither retriever alone is defensible when the other holds a fifth of the answers.

dense.query_prefix: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:

bm25.tokenizer: lowercase; thousands separators removed inside digit runs; split on runs of non-alphanumeric characters
bm25.parameter_sweep_note: k1 in {0.9,1.2,1.5,2.0} x b in {0.5,0.75,1.0} was measured on dev. All twelve combinations produced identical hit@5 and MRR, so the standard defaults are kept and no tuning is claimed.

fusion.k_source: Cormack et al. default, not tuned
fusion.note: RRF reads rank positions only. Dense cosine and BM25 scores are on different unnormalised scales, so any score-level combination would require inventing a weighting.

chunking.note: Selected on dev from {400/80, 600/100, 600/150, 800/120, 1000/150}. Larger chunks keep a provision and its form-identifying context in the same window, which is what the dominant failure mode required.

dev_selection.caveat: 14 answerable dev questions. hit@5 of 1.000 is a small-sample result and should not be expected to hold on the held-out split.

not_implemented.reranker: No cross-encoder or LLM reranker. Dev evidence shows the failure is candidate selection (the right chunk is often absent from the candidate list), not ordering within a good list. A reranker cannot promote what was never retrieved.
not_implemented.query_expansion: None. It would blur the form distinction the benchmark turns on.
not_implemented.metadata_form_filter: Not implemented. Inferring the target form from query wording is feasible, but hybrid fusion already lifts top-document accuracy to parity with BM25, and a filter that guesses wrong removes the correct document entirely.
